author: Show-Me State Times
title: Americans for Tax Reform to Sens. Hawley, Schmitt: The Credit Card Competition Act is 'at the expense of consumers'
text:
Grover Norquist, CEO of Americans for Tax Reform | Wikipedia
Grover Norquist, CEO of Americans for Tax Reform | Wikipedia
The Americans for Tax Reform, a nonprofit advocacy group based in Washington, D.C., has signed a letter opposing renewed efforts to impose price controls on credit cards. The letter was sent to Congress members on January 28.
The Senate Judiciary Committee held a hearing on November 19, 2024, titled "Breaking the Visa-Mastercard Duopoly: Bringing Competition and Lower Fees to the Credit Card System," to discuss the Credit Card Competition Act (CCCA). This hearing included testimony from representatives of Visa, Mastercard, and various stakeholders. The committee examined the potential impacts of the CCCA on the credit card market and consumer fees.
According to the letter, the Credit Card Competition Act is described as "a backdoor price control, and extension and expansion of the Durbin amendment as enacted in the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (P.L. 111-203)." It mentions that the bill would require U.S.-issued credit cards to offer at least two unaffiliated payment network options and prohibit both networks from being Visa and Mastercard due to their dominant market shares. The letter further argues that "the bill also mandates that the proprietary security of the credit cards function so that all networks are available for retailers to pick and choose—consumers get no say whatsoever," criticizing the legislation for failing to mention consumers or explain how they would benefit.
Grover Norquist, CEO of Americans for Tax Reform
| Wikipedia
A 2022 report by the Government Accountability Office (GAO) found that interchange fee caps under the Durbin Amendment led to a significant decline in free checking accounts. According to this report, if not implemented, 65 percent of noninterest checking accounts offered by covered banks would have been free. The GAO noted that banks offset lost interchange fee revenue by increasing other fees, impacting consumers' access to low-cost banking services.
The Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond conducted a study revealing that 98.8 percent of merchants did not pass on savings from reduced debit interchange fees to consumers after implementing the Durbin Amendment. Instead, 21.6 percent of merchants increased prices, suggesting that anticipated consumer benefits did not materialize as intended.
Americans for Tax Reform was founded in 1985 with a focus on advocating for limited government and lower taxes while preserving free market principles. It engages in policy analysis and lobbying efforts to influence tax and economic legislation.
Grover Norquist, CEO of Americans for Tax Reform, delivered this statement in a coalition letter addressed to members of Congress in response to anticipated reintroduction of the Credit Card Competition Act in the 119th Congress. The letter discusses proposals for network routing mandates and interest rate caps, warning they would distort the market and harm consumers.
